normalization_policy: normalized claim plus artifact and evidence target; no voting

findings.claim: The design does not define a legal durable storage and recovery path for the exact sealed AdmissionBundle. It calls prepare read-only while also making that command the bundle write mechanism, forbids every pre-charge write except AdmissionInvalidation, and only requires the charge record to bind a bundle hash. Thus READY can rely on volatile or undeclared evidence and a crash after charge can leave a charged attempt without reproducible proof bytes.
findings.evidence_excerpt: "The sole pre-charge write exception is the coordinator-owned, uncharged append of one immutable `AdmissionInvalidation`"; "the coordinator-owned read-only prepare operation".
findings.impact: A charge can be recorded without a durable, independently verifiable admission proof, or the design requires an undeclared pre-charge write; either defeats the claimed fail-closed evidence boundary and makes crash recovery unverifiable.
findings.recommended_action: Before READY, define under P15 an approved canonical immutable storage or atomic embedding of the complete bundle bytes and validator receipt, including its allowed effect and crash-recovery rule; otherwise require NOT_READY. Do not rely on a hash whose exact bytes are not durably retrievable.

findings.claim: The failed-migration recovery does not require a post-restore raw-byte hash/version equality check against the immutable pre-migration backup. Because the source ledger is explicitly known strict-invalid, rerunning the same strict validator fails whether the original was restored or a different invalid candidate remains, so the stated recovery cannot prove reversibility.
findings.evidence_excerpt: "Because P3 deliberately blocks charging any WBS attempt against the known strict-invalid ledger"; "restores the recorded pre-migration current bytes through the declared owning file operation, reruns the same strict validator".
findings.impact: A failed migration can leave altered loss- or acceptance-bearing ledger bytes while the procedure returns to candidate work, undermining the required backup-first, lossless, deterministic, reversible migration guarantee and contaminating later admission evidence.
findings.recommended_action: Require a version-guarded restore receipt that rehashes the persisted restored path and proves equality to the immutable backup, including attempt/charge/acceptance-reference equality; stop and escalate on mismatch, while recording the expected strict-invalid result separately.

findings.claim: The migration guard says the next P3/P15 admission rejects a ledger whose attempt set or charge count differs from the exact HUMAN-accepted migrated bytes, while the defined first valid commit necessarily allocates an attempt and records cumulative charge. It does not scope equality to the pre-charge source or define a validated append-only lineage for charged successors.
findings.evidence_excerpt: "one attempt allocation, boundary receipt and cumulative charge"; "The next P3/P15 admission rejects any ledger whose selected revision, attempt set, charge count or other acceptance-bearing bytes differ from the exact HUMAN-accepted migrated bytes/hash."
findings.impact: A literal implementation blocks the first or later valid charge; a relaxed implementation has no stated provenance test to distinguish authorized charged successors from altered post-migration ledger state, weakening P3/P15 integrity.
findings.recommended_action: Define separate invariants for the exact pre-charge migrated base and for each candidate/persisted charge: require an authorized, deterministic append-only lineage with version and hash proofs, and state precisely which invariant P3/P15 evaluates at each boundary.

findings.evidence_excerpt: Any alternate acceptor requires a separately recorded HUMAN authority decision before admission; a task-declared rule cannot transfer that authority.
findings.claim: Section 12.7 requires a separately recorded HUMAN authority decision for any alternate acceptor, but no admission invariant or AdmissionBundle receipt enforces it: P2 only requires the closure matrix to declare an acceptance owner, P13 binds only the WBS `wbs_authority` record and allowed effects, and neither Section 6 nor Section 7 defines an acceptance-authority record or predicate.
findings.impact: A plan could name a non-HUMAN or task-declared acceptance owner and still pass P1-P15, letting a non-HUMAN artifact grant acceptance authority that Section 4 reserves to the HUMAN, contrary to must_check 'HUMAN authority remains explicit for ... acceptance'.
findings.recommended_action: Add an admission invariant plus AdmissionBundle receipt binding each task's acceptance owner to the HUMAN decision owner or to an alternate named in a separately recorded, non-revoked HUMAN authority decision, and re-verify that record/scope in P14 at the charge boundary.

findings.evidence_excerpt: | stale/contradictory coordinator, Goal, Team or active work | P8-P10 snapshot agreement |
findings.claim: The counterfactual table maps contradictory state only to 'coordinator, Goal, Team or active work', and P8-P10 plus Section 13 define no predicate comparing the execution ledger's recorded active/paused mission-run state with the runtime goal state, so must_check 'Goal, Team, coordinator, active work and execution ledger state cannot contradict at admission' is not closed even though Section 2.3 lists ledger-vs-goal active/paused disagreement as a contributing condition.
findings.impact: An execution.json recorded as active while the runtime goal is paused (or vice versa) can satisfy P1-P13 and be charged, re-entering the Section 2.3 contributing condition the design claims to close and contradicting must_check item 9.
findings.recommended_action: Add an explicit admission predicate and bundle receipt requiring the ledger's recorded mission/run state and pause-resume marker to equal the runtime goal state at the same observation epoch, with P14 re-observation at the charge boundary.
